title: No Spark — Ignition Failure
shortDescription: Engine will not start because the ignition coil is not producing spark.
fullDescription:
Echo CS-series chainsaws use a magneto ignition with a fixed air gap. E01 is a service-manual code for a no-spark condition. Typical causes are a fouled or worn spark plug, broken stop-switch wire grounding the coil, or a failed coil after years of vibration.

Air gap is 0.008-0.012" between coil and flywheel. Re-gap any time you remove the coil.

fixSteps.title: Test stop switch
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect stop wire from coil and retry spark; if spark returns, switch or wire is shorting.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Set air gap 0.010" with business card when reinstalling.

whenToCallPro: If a sheared flywheel key is suspected, a dealer has the correct puller and torque tools.

title: Fuel Starvation — Carburetor Issue
shortDescription: Engine cranks but will not run more than a few seconds.
fullDescription:
Ethanol degradation of diaphragms in the Walbro/Zama carburetors is the classic Echo problem. E02 represents the cluster of fuel starvation symptoms: starts and dies, no idle, bogs under load.

Fuel lines crack between the tank and carb — check before rebuilding the carb.

causes.cause: Rotten primer bulb or fuel line

fixSteps.title: Replace fuel lines
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fuel and vent lines, primer bulb, and tank pickup filter.

fixSteps.title: Rebuild carb
fixSteps.instruction: Install Echo carb kit — new diaphragms and gaskets.

fixSteps.title: Set H/L screws
fixSteps.instruction: Default H=1, L=1.25 turns out; fine-tune per tachometer.

whenToCallPro: Carb tuning without a tach risks lean-running piston damage — dealers have the proper tools.

faq.q: Can I use 87 octane pump gas?
faq.a: Yes but use premium non-ethanol when possible, mixed at 50:1 with Echo Power Blend oil.

title: Chain Brake Engaged / Safety Stop
shortDescription: Chain brake is engaged — chain will not rotate.
fullDescription:
Echo saws use an inertial chain brake that trips automatically on kickback or when pushed forward by the operator's hand. E03 is the service code for chain refusal to turn due to active brake.

Reset by pulling the brake handle toward the rear handle until it clicks.

causes.cause: Weak brake spring keeping it locked

symptoms: Chain does not rotate at idle or throttle

fixSteps.title: Release brake
fixSteps.instruction: Pull brake handle rearward until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Clean brake area
fixSteps.instruction: Remove clutch cover, blow out sawdust with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Replace spring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace brake spring if weak; requires clutch drum removal.

whenToCallPro: If brake band is worn or stuck, have a dealer replace — getting it wrong reduces safety.

faq.q: Is the brake supposed to stop the chain instantly?
faq.a: Yes — it should stop within 0.15 s of triggering. Test periodically.

title: Air Filter Blocked
shortDescription: Loss of power and smoky exhaust — air filter is plugged.
fullDescription: Sawdust-rich environments plug Echo flocked-foam or pleated-paper filters quickly. E04 reflects the symptom: sluggish acceleration, black exhaust, and 4-stroking (rich burbling) at full throttle.
symptoms: Rich running / burbling at full throttle

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Tap out dust; wash foam in warm soapy water, dry completely before reinstalling.

fixSteps.title: Inspect boot
fixSteps.instruction: Check the intake rubber boot for cracks; replace if split.

faq.a: No — Echo uses dry foam. Oil will restrict airflow.

title: Bar Oil Not Flowing
shortDescription: Chain runs dry — oiler pump not delivering bar oil.
fullDescription:
Echo chainsaws use a worm-driven adjustable oiler. E05 symptomatically covers chain-burn conditions. Common causes are empty oil tank, plugged oil galley, or a cracked oil pickup line in the tank.

Never run a saw without bar oil — the chain will stretch and the bar will blue within one tank of fuel.
symptoms: Oil tank full but no flow to bar

fixSteps.title: Verify oil
fixSteps.instruction: Fill with quality bar-and-chain oil (Echo Premium 2100).

fixSteps.title: Clean bar/groove
fixSteps.instruction: Remove bar, clean groove with a flat tool, clear oil hole in bar.

fixSteps.title: Replace pickup line
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve pickup from tank, swap cracked line and filter.

whenToCallPro: Oiler pump replacement is fiddly — dealer service avoids shortcuts.

faq.a: In emergency only — motor oil lacks tack additives and slings off. Use bar-and-chain oil.

title: Engine Overheating / Seizure Risk
shortDescription: Engine running excessively hot — risk of piston seizure.
fullDescription: Two-stroke saws overheat quickly if run lean, low on mix oil, or with blocked cylinder fins. E06 is the cluster of overheat symptoms — seized piston, scored cylinder, or no-start after shutdown while hot.

fixSteps.title: Stop immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Shut down engine and let cool 30 minutes before inspection.

fixSteps.title: Verify fuel mix
fixSteps.instruction: Re-mix 50:1 with correct 2-stroke oil; drain old mix if uncertain.

fixSteps.title: Compression test
fixSteps.instruction: Healthy saw reads 120+ PSI. Under 90 PSI = piston damage likely.

whenToCallPro: Compression below 90 PSI or scored cylinder needs pro rebuild or replacement.

faq.a: 50:1 with Echo Power Blend or equivalent TCW-3 2-stroke oil.

title: Starter Recoil Failure
shortDescription: Starter rope won't retract, or pulls limply without cranking the engine.
fullDescription:
The recoil assembly contains a spring, pulley, and pawls. E07 covers broken recoil spring, broken starter rope, or failed pawls that no longer catch the flywheel.

Recoil spring replacement is DIY-able with care — wear safety glasses when handling.
symptoms: Rope pulls out loose (no engine rotation)

fixSteps.title: Disassemble recoil
fixSteps.instruction: Remove starter cover, carefully release tension before unwinding.

fixSteps.title: Replace spring and rope
fixSteps.instruction: Install new spring (wear glasses), thread new rope, wind pulley 6 turns before securing.

fixSteps.title: Replace pawls
fixSteps.instruction: If worn, swap pawls and return springs on the flywheel side.

whenToCallPro: If nervous about spring handling — dealer service is quick and inexpensive.

faq.a: Rope fatigues over years — UV and vibration weaken the fibers.

title: Chain Tension Loss
shortDescription: Chain sags on bar — improperly tensioned or worn drive sprocket.
fullDescription: New chains stretch rapidly during the first hour of use. E08 covers improper tension symptoms: derailed chain, bar damage, and poor cuts. Also flags a worn rim-sprocket which cannot hold pitch.

fixSteps.title: Retension chain
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen bar nuts, lift bar tip, turn tensioner until chain snaps back to bar. Retorque bar nuts.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sprocket
fixSteps.instruction: Replace rim sprocket every second chain; wear mark = 0.020" grooves.

faq.a: Chain should snap back when pulled, with no sag under the bar.

title: Clogged Muffler / Spark Arrestor
shortDescription: Loss of power due to blocked exhaust.
fullDescription: Echo exhausts include a mesh spark arrestor that clogs with carbon. E09 covers symptoms of power loss, high RPM only at no-load, and excessive heat. Clean or replace the arrestor at every 50 hours.
symptoms: Loss of top RPM under load

fixSteps.title: Remove screen
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew end cap; remove spark arrestor screen.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Burn carbon off with a torch, or install new screen.

faq.q: Can I just remove the screen?
faq.a: Illegal in most US states and on public lands — use a clean screen.

title: Throttle Trigger / Interlock Fault
shortDescription: Throttle does not open, or safety trigger interlock is stuck.
fullDescription: Echo uses a two-lever trigger: the safety latch on the top of the rear handle must be depressed before the main throttle can move. E10 covers a sticky interlock, a broken return spring, or a bent throttle link.

fixSteps.title: Clean rear handle
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out debris with compressed air; work latch to free.

fixSteps.title: Inspect linkage
fixSteps.instruction: Open handle half, inspect return spring and throttle link.

fixSteps.title: Replace parts
fixSteps.instruction: Swap broken springs or bent link.

whenToCallPro: Usually DIY — dealer only if the carb link is internally broken.

faq.a: Never — it prevents unintended chain rotation and injury.
